content.question: What does the numeric value (e.g., 160) shown in the layout editor usually represent?

options.text: A margin or spacing value from the top or other edges

content.explanation: The instructor mentions that the 160 value is just a margin from the top; it's the spacing between elements or edges when nothing else is specified.

content.question: Why is an ID compared to an enrollment number in the transcript?

options.text: Both are used for payment processing

content.explanation: An ID uniquely identifies a view in the layout, similar to how an enrollment number uniquely identifies a student.

content.question: What mistake causes red squiggly lines, and when do those errors become build-stopping?

options.text: Missing an ID always stops the build
Missing mandatory attributes like layout_width/layout_height will cause build failures; other small issues show squiggles but may not stop build
Any color change causes a crash
Changing text content stops the build

content.explanation: Red squiggles can indicate minor issues, but the app fails to build when essential attributes (layout_width/layout_height) are missing.

content.question: Which action explains how to attach a view's constraint to another view's edge?

options.text: Drag from the constraint anchor of the child to the target anchor of the other view

content.explanation: The instructor demonstrates dragging the anchor point from one view to another to create a constraint link between their edges.

content.question: Review question: From Section 2, which tag displays text on screen in Android XML?
content.explanation: TextView is the standard Android XML component used to display text on the user interface.
